title: Patient Hardship Discount Program Terms for Applicants: Reapplying After an Income Denial
content:
**Patient Hardship Discount Program — terms for applicants.** After a denial for income above the limit, a new income-tested application is accepted no earlier than the reapplication wait, in calendar days, after the date of that denial. Days are counted as calendar days from the denial date, the denial date itself being day zero.

### The terms explained

- **What starts the clock.** A denial of the applicant's earlier application for the reason *income above the limit*. The date of that denial is the determination date shown on the denied case in the program's records for the same applicant; the records, not the applicant's recollection, fix that date.
- **What is measured.** A new application at an income-tested level: Hardship Discount Level 1 (25%), Level 2 (50%), Level 3 (75%), Level 4 (100%) or Catastrophic Medical Hardship. At each of these levels the reapplication wait is 90 calendar days.
- **How days are counted.** Calendar days, with the denial date as day zero, so the day after the denial is day one.
- **The boundary.** "No earlier than" means the application is accepted on the last day of the wait itself and on any later day; on any day before it, it is not accepted.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

A denial for income above the limit is dated 2026-03-02, and the wait is 90 calendar days.

| Date of the new income-tested application | Day count from the denial date | Accepted under this term |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-03-02 | Day 0 | No |
| 2026-05-30 | Day 89 | No |
| 2026-05-31 | Day 90 | Yes |
| 2026-06-15 | Day 105 | Yes |

### In plain terms

An applicant whose income was found above the limit waits until day 90 after the denial date before a new income-tested application is accepted; on day 90 itself the application is on time.
